Manila City Mayor @IskoMoreno is calling for local government units (LGUs) to take over the operation and maintenance of flood control facilities, saying the current system under national agencies has failed to address flooding effectively.

Speaking before members of the Association of Philippine Journalists – Samahang Plaridel Foundation, Inc., Domagoso stressed that accountability would be clearer if LGUs were in charge. “If you give the mayor the authority, you get action and accountability,” he said. “Let us handle it—because we face the people every day. And when we fail, there’s no one else to blame.”

Domagoso cited the Sunog Apog pumping station in Tondo as an example, saying the newly built facility remains non-functional. “It’s brand new and unusable. Brand new and ineffective. Brand new and not functioning. You name it,” he said.

The mayor argued that turning over the operations to LGUs would ensure direct responsibility. “If you let the mayor run it and it fails, there’s direct responsibility. In three years, if we mess up, we’re done,” he said. “Tama si Presidente, ‘wag na tayo magbolahan. Alam niya ang congressman pinakikialaman ang DPWH project.”

Domagoso also commended the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (@MMDA) for operating 72 pumping stations across Metro Manila, including 24 in Manila. He contrasted these with DPWH-constructed stations, which he said are either incomplete or have yet to meet quality standards.

“Buti pa ‘yung sa MMDA tumatakbo,” Domagoso said, also pointing to unfinished projects such as the Estero de Abad, Remedios, and Padre Faura pumping stations.

Domagoso noted that the DPWH has a ₱34 billion flood control budget for Metro Manila, while the MMDA runs its pumping stations with only ₱2 billion annually. He also backed President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s statement in his State of the Nation Address, where the President criticized lapses in flood control programs and vowed to pursue those responsible for failed projects.

#BREAKING 🔥❗️🌊🌐 

A powerful 8.7-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula, triggering tsunami warnings across the Pacific. 

Alerts have been issued for Russia, Japan, Guam, Hawaii, Alaska, and the entire U.S. West Coast, including Oregon, California, and Washington. Japan has ordered evacuations along its coast, with a 12 feet tsunami detected in Hokkaido. The Philippines and Indonesia are also on high alert.

Significant aftershocks, including 5.5, 5.8, and 6.0-magnitude quakes, continue to shake Kamchatka. 

In Hawaii, heavy traffic is reported in Honolulu as thousands evacuate to higher ground, with unconfirmed reports predicting potential flooding up to 27 feet ( 9 meters) 

Japan has suspended train services in Tokyo and Yokohama due to the tsunami threat. 

The earthquake, the strongest in the region since 1952, has caused rapid water recession in Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky Bay, exposing the seabed. 

The entire Pacific region remains on high alert as the situation develops.

data.text:
🇷🇺🇯🇵🇺🇸M8.8 Kamchatka Quake Triggers Mass Evacuations as Tsunami Waves Threaten Japan, Hawaii, Alaska 

❗️A colossal 8.8-magnitude earthquake struck off Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula, Tuesday night  triggering widespread panic and massive evacuations across the North Pacific. 

❗️The quake, one of the strongest ever recorded, unleashed tsunami waves surging toward Japan, Hawaii, and Alaska, with officials warning of catastrophic impacts. 

❗️In Japan, nearly 2 million people fled coastal areas as the Meteorological Agency forecasted waves up to 12 feet hitting Hokkaido and eastern Honshu. Hawaii’s coastline was evacuated, with sirens blaring and residents urged to seek higher ground as waves up to 8 feet struck Oahu and Maui. Alaska and parts of the U.S. West Coast, including Northern California, faced tsunami advisories, with evacuations in low-lying areas. 

❗️The U.S. Embassy in Tokyo was ordered to evacuate, underscoring the crisis’s severity. In Russia’s Kamchatka region, 3,000 people were displaced as waves flooded Severo-Kurilsk, damaging buildings and infrastructure. No fatalities have been reported, but aftershocks up to 7.5 are expected for weeks. 

❗️Pacific nations, including Chile, Peru, and the Philippines, issued alerts for dangerous currents and potential flooding, urging residents to stay vigilant.
